title: A step-by-step protocol for performing LIVE-PAINT super-resolution imaging of proteins in live cells using reversible peptide-protein interactions
protocol: Prepare a stock of synthetic complete media with 6.7 g/L yeast nitrogen base and amino acids, plus 10 g/L raffinose and the desired concentration of galactose.
Pipette 600 μL of synthetic complete media into a culture tube.
Pick one yeast colony from an agar plate into the media.
Mix to evenly distribute the cells in the media.
Prepare a second aliquot of 400 μL synthetic complete media in a culture tube.
Add 100 μL of cells from the first suspension to the fresh 400 μL aliquot, making a 1:5 dilution.
Grow the cultures overnight at 30°C in a shaking incubator.
Use a TIRF microscope equipped with a 488 nm laser and fitted with a ‘perfect focus’ system.
Rotate the mirrors in the beamline path to align the laser parallel to the optical axis.
Mount a 1.49 NA TIRF objective on an inverted Nikon TI2 microscope.
Use an appropriate camera to collect fluorescence output from the microscope.
Clean 22 x 22 mm glass coverslips with thickness no. 1 using a 20 minute exposure in a Zepto plasma laboratory unit.
Secure frame-seal slide chambers to a cleaned coverslip by removing one plastic side and attaching it gently to make a secure seal.
Prepare the slide surface for yeast cell attachment by coating it with approximately 100 μL of 2 mg/mL concanavalin A dissolved in PBS pH 7.4.
Leave the concanavalin A on the slide surface for 30 seconds, then pipette off excess liquid, tilting the slide to ensure all liquid is removed.
Pipette 150 μL of yeast overnight culture grown to mid-log phase (OD 0.1-0.5) onto the slide.
Leave the yeast culture on the slide for approximately 5 minutes.
Pipette off the culture media, removing cells which are not bound to the slide.
Wash the surface three times by pipetting 150 μL of synthetic complete media onto the slide, pipetting up and down a few times, and then discarding the media.
Add 150 μL fresh synthetic complete media to the slide before imaging.
Mount the slide containing yeast cells on the microscope by placing the slide on top of a drop of immersion oil on the objective.
Set the desired exposure time and laser power for the experiments.
Bring the sample into focus and then adjust the laser angle to achieve TIRF.
Image the cells in TIRF for the desired amount of time.
Ensure individual blinking events can be seen during imaging.
Vary the TIRF angle, increase laser power, or allow fluorescent proteins to photobleach if single blinking events are not visible.
Save output as a tiff stack.
Load a tiff stack into Fiji for image analysis.
Use Peak Fit function of the Fiji GDSC SMLM plugin to analyze localization events.
Set typical parameters including signal strength threshold of 30, minimum photon threshold of 100, and precision threshold of 20 nm.
